title: A child under age 1 should ride rear-facing, and stay rear-facing until the seat's own limit
summary: NHTSA says a child under age 1 should always ride rear-facing, and should stay rear-facing until the seat's height or weight limit.
body: NHTSA says a rear-facing seat has a harness and, in a crash, cradles and moves with the child to reduce stress on a young neck and spinal cord. For birth to 12 months, a child under age 1 should always ride rear-facing. Infant-only seats are rear-facing only. Convertible seats often allow a higher limit, so the child can stay rear-facing longer. From 1 to 3 years, the page says to keep the child rear-facing as long as possible, until the child reaches the top height or weight the maker allows, and only then to move to a forward-facing seat with a harness and tether. Under age 1 is the page's hard line. The later limit is the seat's own label, not a single birthday. This is US guidance.
